title: Internal admin provisioning + group mapping for RBAC v2 (break-glass included)
text:
Internal admin provisioning + group mapping for RBAC v2 (break-glass included)

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Mar 10, 2025 at 9:12 AM PT
Subject: Internal admin provisioning + group mapping for RBAC v2 (break-glass included)

Marcus,

As we get closer to dogfood + pilots, I want to lock down how we provision *internal* admin access under RBAC v2 (SSO group mapping, separation of duties, and break-glass).

Current state (RBAC v1):
- We have a couple of “super-admin” internal users who effectively bypass in Console / Control Plane.
- Access is not consistently expressed via groups, and it’s hard to evidence “least privilege” to customers.

Proposal for RBAC v2 (high level):
1) All privileged access for employees comes from IdP groups (Okta) -> Redwood role bindings.
2) No standing “global admin” for prod customer orgs. If we need access, it’s time-bound break-glass with approvals + audit trail.
3) Keep internal tenant (“Redwood Internal”) separate from customer tenants. Internal operational work should happen in internal tenant wherever possible.

Concrete questions I need Security Eng input on:
A) Group taxonomy: do we want a small number of coarse groups (“IT Admin”, “Security Admin”, “Support ReadOnly”) or more fine-grained (“Audit Export Admin”, “Org/User Admin”, “Routing Policy Operator”, etc.)?
B) How strict are we on separation of duties for employees? e.g., should “Billing Admin” be mutually exclusive with “Security Admin”? (Some of the enterprise questionnaires are explicitly asking.)
C) Break-glass: minimum viable workflow that meets evidence requirements (approver set, max duration, alerts). I’m aligning with the Confluence draft, but we need the practical “who can approve at 2am” answer.

I attached a strawman mapping doc (v0.3) with:
- Proposed Okta group names
- Proposed Redwood roles/templates to map to
- Suggested scope defaults (org vs project vs env)
- Break-glass “elevation” flow

Attachment: RBACv2-Internal-Admin-Provisioning-v0.3.docx

If we can agree on the above this week, I can get IT provisioning + access reviews aligned before the next internal rollout.

Thanks,
David

—
David Kim
Identity & IT Systems
Redwood Inference


----

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Mar 10, 2025 at 11:05 AM PT
Subject: Re: Internal admin provisioning + group mapping for RBAC v2 (break-glass included)

David,

This is the right direction. A few Security Eng constraints / preferences:

A) Group taxonomy
- Prefer *fewer* Okta groups, but *not* a single “super-admin” bucket.
- Recommended split (minimum):
  1) Redwood-IT-OrgUserAdmin (manage users, role bindings, SSO mappings) — scoped to Redwood Internal org by default
  2) Redwood-Security-AuditAdmin (view/export audit logs, manage retention config) — scope: org (internal + customer orgs if explicitly granted)
  3) Redwood-Platform-DeploymentOperator (routing/model pinning/rollout changes) — scope: environment/cluster where possible
  4) Redwood-Support-ReadOnlyAuditor (read-only in Console + audit log view, NO key/secret ops)

Rationale: we can show separation of duties and avoid the “support can rotate keys” concern that comes up in customer reviews.

B) Separation of duties
- Strong recommendation: Security-AuditAdmin should not also be OrgUserAdmin by default.
- Billing is out of band from this thread, but yes: billing admin should not have ability to change auth settings.

C) Break-glass
- Requirements I’m holding the line on:
  - time-bound elevation (default 60 min, max 4 hours)
  - approval by 2 people (one must be Security). For after-hours, can be Security on-call + IT on-call.
  - alerting to SecOps channel and recorded ticket (we can use INT-19103 style template).
  - *no* “permanent” break-glass membership in privileged groups.

One nuance: for Private deployments, customers may require *their* approval for any vendor access. We should bake that into the guidance (even if the mechanism is “customer runs the command” for air-gapped). But for Hosted/Dedicated we can implement internal break-glass as above.

Can you update the strawman doc to incorporate this split and call out default scoping? Happy to review again.

Marcus

—
Marcus Lin
Security Engineering Lead
Redwood Inference


----

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Mar 10, 2025 at 2:30 PM PT
Subject: Re: Internal admin provisioning + group mapping for RBAC v2 (break-glass included)

Got it.

A couple of follow-ups / operational details to make sure we don’t paint ourselves into a corner:

1) Scope defaults
If we set Okta group mappings to “Redwood Internal org only” by default, we still need a controlled way to bind someone to a *customer org* when necessary.
- Are we expecting a manual role-binding created in Console (or API) per incident?
- If yes, do we require that binding creation itself be break-glass, or can OrgUserAdmin do it while still being scoped to a customer org?

2) “DeploymentOperator” scope granularity
Our current tenancy model is “org -> project -> environment”, but Dedicated/Private also introduces “cluster”.
- For MVP, would Security accept environment-scoped role bindings (even if cluster-level is the real desired end state), provided we log the scope and have an explicit ticket?

3) Evidence / access reviews
IT can do quarterly access reviews on Okta groups easily.
- For break-glass role bindings (created ad-hoc), do you want a weekly report sent to GRC (Olga) / Aisha for review? Or do we just rely on audit logs + INT tickets?

I can implement the group names as you suggested. My goal is: no more direct user allowlists, everything via group membership + time-bound bindings.

Thanks,
David


----

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Mar 11, 2025 at 9:02 AM PT
Subject: Re: Internal admin provisioning + group mapping for RBAC v2 (break-glass included)

Answering inline.

On Mon, Mar 10, 2025 at 2:30 PM David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> 1) Scope defaults
> If we set Okta group mappings to “Redwood Internal org only” by default, we still need a controlled way to bind someone to a customer org when necessary.
> - Are we expecting a manual role-binding created in Console (or API) per incident?
> - If yes, do we require that binding creation itself be break-glass, or can OrgUserAdmin do it while still being scoped to a customer org?

We should treat “grant employee access to customer org” as break-glass in itself.
- Flow I want: open incident/support ticket -> request break-glass -> Security approves -> system creates time-bound role binding scoped to the customer org (and ideally the specific project/env).
- OrgUserAdmin should not be able to self-serve bindings into customer orgs without an approval trail.

> 2) “DeploymentOperator” scope granularity
> - For MVP, would Security accept environment-scoped role bindings (even if cluster-level is the real desired end state), provided we log the scope and have an explicit ticket?

Yes for MVP, with two caveats:
- The permission set for DeploymentOperator must not include user/role management or key/secret management.
- Logging must include: employee identity, scope, permission, decision, and “reason/ticket id” field. (This is part of the authz decision logging workstream.)

> 3) Evidence / access reviews
> - For break-glass role bindings (created ad-hoc), do you want a weekly report sent to GRC (Olga) / Aisha for review? Or do we just rely on audit logs + INT tickets?

Weekly report during pilot. After we’re stable, we can move to monthly. Audit logs alone are not enough because reviewers won’t query raw logs.
- Suggest: automated digest (past 7 days): who elevated, what org, duration, ticket link, and whether elevation was revoked on time.

Also: please make sure IT group membership changes are logged and retained. We’ve already had one internal issue where someone lost Console access unexpectedly (INT-19022), and we need to separate “authz deny” vs “SSO group missing.”

Marcus


----

From: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Mar 11, 2025 at 10:18 AM PT
Subject: Re: Internal admin provisioning + group mapping for RBAC v2 (break-glass included)

Agree with Marcus’s approach.

Two exec-level constraints to incorporate:
1) “No standing access to customer environments” needs to be true in practice, not just policy. So: time-bound + review + alerting are non-negotiable.
2) For any customer-facing security review, we should be able to articulate separation of duties plainly (Support read-only, Security audit/export, Platform operator) and show that employee access is approval-based.

David — please update the doc and send me the final group list + the proposed break-glass approval roster (names/roles) for sign-off. I also want to confirm we have an on-call rotation that can fulfill the “Security approver” requirement.

Aisha

—
Dr. Aisha Rahman
Chief Information Security Officer
Redwood Inference
